name: Merge Overlapping Interval
statement:
1. You are given a number n, representing the number of time-intervals.
2. In the next n lines, you are given a pair of space separated numbers.
3. The pair of numbers represent the start time and end time of a meeting (first number is start time and second number is end time)
4. You are required to merge the meetings and print the merged meetings output in increasing order of start time.

E.g. Let us say there are 6 meetings
1 8
5 12
14 19
22 28
25 27
27 30

Then the output of merged meetings will belongs
1 12
14 19
22 30

Note -> The given input maynot be sorted by start-time.
outputFormat:
Print a merged meeting start time and end time separated by a space in a line
.. print all merged meetings one in each line.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 10^4
0 <= ith start time < 100
ith start time < ith end time <= 100

templates.python:
def mergeOverlappingIntervals(arr):

      arr = [ ]

                           narr.append(int(inp[1]))
                           arr.append(narr)

editorial:
We will follow out what, how and why approach.

We are given this meeting array including the starting and ending time of meetings and we have to merge it.

22 28

1 8

25 27

14 19

27 30

5 12

Logic:

Sort the array in increasing start time of meeting.

1. First element to be pushed into the stack

2. Compare start time of second element with end time of first element, if it is less then we will merge the two and if not then we will directly push it.

3. If we know that we have to merge then also we have to check that whether our end time of meeting will be updated or not.

4. During merge: If the end time of second element is greater than the first then we will update the end time, merge the two elements and push it.

5. During merge: if the end time is lesser than the first elements end time then we will not push anything in the stack. It is obvious that second element is already a part of the first element.

6. We will repeat the comparison steps for every element.

7. At last we will push the elements into a different stack as according to question we have to print the answers in increasing order of start time of meetings.

Example-

The first step we follow will be that we will be sorting this array.

1 8

5 12

14 19

22 28

25 27

27 30

Now we will push the first element into the stack.

For the second element we can see that 5<8 and 12>8 so it will merge with 1-8 and we will get the interval as 1-12 which will be pushed into the stack.

Now for 14-19 we can clearly see that 14>12 so it will be directly pushed into the stack.

Again 22>19, it will be directly pushed.

Now we have 25-27. We can see that 25<28 but 27<28 too so this interval is already present in 22-18 and here no change in the end time will take place.

Lastly we have 27-30. 27<28 and 30>28 so it will merger and will become 22-30 and will be pushed into the stack.

Now we will transfer the elements of stack1 to stack2

Now we will pop and print.

1 - 12

14 - 19

22 - 30

This is working because we have sorted the array first and then we are comparing the values.

NOTE: In the code we have taken this array as array of objects and to sort it we have to implement Comparable interface because java does not allow us to sort it like we sort the integer array.
